tools.name: brainkb_login
tools.description:
Authenticate to BrainKB with the user's credentials and cache the JWT for
    THIS session only (isolated per caller). The password/token are never echoed.

    Uses single sign-on: one login mints a refresh token, cached for THIS session,
    which is exchanged on demand for per-service access toke

tools.name: brainkb_globus_login
tools.description:
Start an OAuth login (Globus / ORCID / GitHub) for THIS session — use this
    instead of brainkb_login when the user signs in with Globus rather than a
    password. Returns a URL to open in a browser; after signing in, the page shows
    a short one-time code — pass it to brainkb_finish_login(code

tools.name: brainkb_finish_login
tools.description:
Complete an OAuth login started with brainkb_globus_login by exchanging the
    one-time code shown in the browser for a session token. The code is single-use
    and never echoed back.

tools.name: brainkb_logout
tools.description: Forget the cached token for this session.

tools.name: brainkb_whoami
tools.description:
Report the current caller's auth state (email, authenticated, and when the
    cached session expires). When signed in it also returns base_url — the backend
    THIS SERVER talks to, which on a hosted deployment is an internal address and
    says nothing about the caller's own machine.

tools.name: brainkb_create_token
tools.description:
Generate a Personal Access Token (PAT) for browser-free auth. Requires you
    to be logged in already (brainkb_login or brainkb_globus_login). The token is
    shown ONCE and never again — copy it and set it as BRAINKB_TOKEN in your
    MCP/skill config; then no login or browser is needed until it

tools.name: brainkb_list_tokens
tools.description:
List your Personal Access Tokens (metadata only — the secret is never
    shown): id, name, prefix, created/last-used/expiry, and whether each is
    active/revoked/expired. Use the id with brainkb_revoke_token.

tools.name: brainkb_revoke_token
tools.description:
Revoke one of your Personal Access Tokens by id (see brainkb_list_tokens).
    Takes effect immediately — the next call using that token fails.

tools.name: brainkb_use_token
tools.description:
Use a Personal Access Token (brainkb_pat_...) for THIS session — an
    alternative to setting BRAINKB_TOKEN in the config. Validates the token, then
    caches it so subsequent calls authenticate with it. The token is never echoed.

tools.name: brainkb_list_spaces
tools.description:
List spaces the user can see (their own/member spaces + public ones), each
    annotated with THIS caller's permission so you know what they may do:
      - your_role: 'owner' | 'editor' | 'viewer' | null (their space membership)
      - is_owner:  they own the space
      - access:    'owner' | 'me

tools.name: brainkb_create_space
tools.description:
Create a workspace/space. The caller becomes owner.
    slug: lowercase/hyphen id, **globally unique** — if it's already taken the call
    returns 409 (pick another slug; slugs are never reused/deleted).
    visibility: 'private' or 'public';
    description: short human description (recommended —

tools.name: brainkb_set_space_visibility
tools.description:
Set a space 'public' (anyone, even anonymous, can read) or 'private'
    (members only). Owner only.

tools.name: brainkb_add_space_member
tools.description: Add/update a space member. role: 'owner' | 'editor' | 'viewer'. Owner only.

tools.name: brainkb_add_space_graph
tools.description:
Register a named graph and bind it to a space, so ingest/read on that graph
    are governed by the space's membership and visibility. Owner/editor only.
    The named_graph_iri is **globally unique** — one graph belongs to exactly one
    space. If it's already registered (to any space) the call re

tools.name: brainkb_ingest_text
tools.description:
Ingest raw RDF text (Turtle / N-Triples / JSON-LD, auto-detected) into a
    named graph. Returns a job_id; ingestion runs in the background — poll with
    brainkb_job_status. The graph must be registered (see brainkb_add_space_graph)
    and the caller must have write access to its space.

    `sh

tools.name: brainkb_list_uploads
tools.description:
List RDF files YOU have staged with POST /upload but not yet ingested.

    Shows each upload_id, its size, sha256 and when it expires. Only your own
    uploads are visible.

tools.name: brainkb_upload_status
tools.description:
State of one of your staged/submitted uploads.

    `state` is `staged` (waiting for brainkb_ingest_upload), `submitting` (the server
    is streaming it to the ingest API), `submitted` (accepted — `job_id` is set, poll
    brainkb_job_status) or `failed` (the staged bytes were KEPT, so retry with

tools.name: brainkb_discard_upload
tools.description: Delete one of your staged uploads without ingesting it.

tools.name: brainkb_ingest_upload
tools.description:
Ingest a file you staged with `POST /upload` into a named graph.

    This is the route for a large local file: your HTTP client streams the bytes
    straight to this server over HTTPS, then you name the resulting upload_id here. The
    server reads its own staged copy and posts it to the ingest A

tools.name: brainkb_ingest_files
tools.description:
Ingest local RDF files (ttl/nt/nq/rdf/owl/jsonld/json) into a named graph.
    Returns a job_id; runs in the background — poll with brainkb_job_status.

tools.name: brainkb_list_jobs
tools.description: List the user's ingest jobs (newest first) with status and progress.

tools.name: brainkb_job_status
tools.description:
Detailed status of one ingest job: status, progress %, current file/stage,
    per-file failures, and (when complete) a summary.

tools.name: brainkb_recover_job
tools.description: Attempt to recover a stuck/errored ingest job (marks it recoverable/errored).

tools.name: brainkb_search
tools.description:
Full-text search over the knowledge graphs, access-filtered by space
    visibility. Pass `space` to scope to one workspace, omit for a full search.
    Anonymous/other users never see private-space data.

tools.name: brainkb_read_space
tools.description:
Read all RDF (JSON-LD) in a space's graphs. Public spaces are readable by
    anyone; private spaces require membership.

tools.name: brainkb_list_registered_graphs
tools.description:
List registered named graphs visible to the caller (private-space graphs the
    caller can't access are hidden).

tools.name: brainkb_sparql
tools.description:
Run an arbitrary SPARQL query. Requires an Admin/SuperAdmin role (the
    sparql_admin capability) — for ordinary questions prefer brainkb_search,
    brainkb_read_space, or the provenance/delta tools, which need no admin role.

tools.name: brainkb_provenance_job
tools.description: PROV-O provenance bundle (JSON-LD) for one ingest job.

tools.name: brainkb_provenance_graph
tools.description: PROV-O ingestion/activity history (JSON-LD) for a named graph.

tools.name: brainkb_delta
tools.description: The exact triples a job added (its delta), as JSON-LD.

tools.name: brainkb_delta_history
tools.description:
A named graph's change history: one entry per ingest delta (job, triple
    count, timestamp), newest first.

tools.name: brainkb_delta_compare
tools.description: Compare two jobs' deltas: A-only / B-only / shared triple counts + triples.

tools.name: brainkb_capabilities
tools.description:
(Admin only) Show a user's roles, effective capabilities, and delegated
    grants. Useful to check why someone can/can't create team spaces, ingest, etc.

tools.name: brainkb_grant_capability
tools.description:
(Admin only) Delegate a capability to a user — e.g. 'create_team_space' or
    'manage_team_space' so a Curator/Lab Member can create/manage team spaces.
    Grantable: create_private_space, create_team_space, manage_team_space, ingest,
    recover, read_private (NOT the admin-only 'grant'/'sparql_a

tools.name: brainkb_revoke_capability
tools.description: (Admin only) Revoke a previously granted capability from a user.

tools.name: brainkb_list_capabilities
tools.description:
(Admin only) Catalog of all KG capabilities, which are delegatable
    ('grantable'), which are admin-only, and a description of each. Use this to see
    the available permission options before granting to a user or group/role.

tools.name: brainkb_role_capabilities
tools.description:
(Admin only) List the capabilities granted to a role/group (e.g.
    'uk_collaborator', 'Lab Member').

tools.name: brainkb_grant_role_capability
tools.description:
(Admin only) Grant a capability to a whole role/group so EVERY member gets
    it — e.g. give a custom group 'uk_collaborator' the 'ingest' or
    'create_private_space' capability. Grantable: create_private_space,
    create_team_space, manage_team_space, ingest, recover, read_private (NOT the

tools.name: brainkb_revoke_role_capability
tools.description: (Admin only) Revoke a capability from a role/group.

tools.name: brainkb_list_access_rules
tools.description: List a space's fine-grained access rules (member/manager of the space).

tools.name: brainkb_add_access_rule
tools.description:
(Space manager) Restrict a space action to a subject.
    action: 'read' | 'write' | 'manage'.
    subject_type: 'global_role' (e.g. 'Admin','Lab Member') | 'member' (an email) |
    'space_role' ('viewer'|'editor'|'owner', matched as >=).
    When rules exist for an action, only matching callers ma

tools.name: brainkb_remove_access_rule
tools.description:
(Space manager) Delete a fine-grained access rule by its id
    (see brainkb_list_access_rules).

tools.name: brainkb_list_users
tools.description:
(Admin) List users (profiles) — filter by `q` (name/email/orcid) or `role`.
    Shows profile_id, email, roles, providers, ban status.

tools.name: brainkb_available_roles
tools.description: (Admin) List the available roles/groups (Admin, Lab Member, Curator, …).

tools.name: brainkb_create_role
tools.description:
(Admin) Create a new role/group — e.g. an 'External' collaborator group —
    which can then be assigned with brainkb_assign_role.

tools.name: brainkb_assign_role
tools.description:
(Admin) Assign a role/group to a user by email (e.g. 'Lab Member', 'External',
    or a custom group). The user must already have a profile (created on first
    login/registration). NOTE: assigning the 'Admin'/'SuperAdmin' role is
    SuperAdmin-only (hierarchy: SuperAdmin > Admin).

tools.name: brainkb_remove_role
tools.description: (Admin) Remove a role/group from a user by email.

tools.name: brainkb_activate_user
tools.description: (Admin) Activate a user's account (sets the JWT user active) by email.

tools.name: brainkb_deactivate_user
tools.description: (Admin) Deactivate a user's account by email.

tools.name: brainkb_ban_user
tools.description:
(Admin) Ban a user by email (reversible; preserves history). This is how
    accounts are removed — there is NO hard delete. Banning an Admin is
    SuperAdmin-only; SuperAdmin accounts cannot be banned.

tools.name: brainkb_unban_user
tools.description: (Admin) Lift a ban on a user by email.

tools.name: brainkb_list_permissions
tools.description:
(Admin) List all usermanagement permissions (resource/action pairs used for
    page-access and role-permission mapping). These are the addable 'permission'
    options; KG action-capabilities are listed by brainkb_list_capabilities.

tools.name: brainkb_create_permission
tools.description:
(Admin) Create a new usermanagement permission, e.g.
    name='dataset.export', resource='dataset', action='export'. Attach it to roles
    via the usermanagement role-permissions API.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: brainkb_globus_login, brainkb_list_uploads, brainkb_ingest_upload, brainkb_add_access_rule, brainkb_list_users · Private data: brainkb_login, brainkb_globus_login, brainkb_finish_login, brainkb_logout, brainkb_create_token, brainkb_list_tokens, brainkb_revoke_token, brainkb_use_token, brainkb_create_space, brainkb_set_space_visibility, brainkb_ingest_text, brainkb_list_uploads, brainkb_ingest_upload, brainkb_ingest_files, brainkb_job_status, brainkb_search, brainkb_read_space, brainkb_list_registered_graphs · Public sink: brainkb_login, brainkb_whoami, brainkb_ingest_text, brainkb_list_uploads, brainkb_upload_status, brainkb_discard_upload, brainkb_ingest_upload, brainkb_add_access_rule, brainkb_list_users, brainkb_assign_role, brainkb_remove_role, brainkb_activate_user, brainkb_deactivate_user, brainkb_ban_user, brainkb_unban_user · Destructive: brainkb_add_space_graph, brainkb_ingest_text, brainkb_discard_upload, brainkb_sparql, brainkb_remove_access_rule, brainkb_remove_role, brainkb_ban_user.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: brainkb_globus_login, brainkb_list_uploads, brainkb_ingest_upload, brainkb_add_access_rule, brainkb_list_users · Private data: brainkb_login, brainkb_globus_login, brainkb_finish_login, brainkb_logout, brainkb_create_token, brainkb_list_tokens, brainkb_revoke_token, brainkb_use_token, brainkb_create_space, brainkb_set_space_visibility, brainkb_ingest_text, brainkb_list_uploads, brainkb_ingest_upload, brainkb_ingest_files, brainkb_job_status, brainkb_search, brainkb_read_space, brainkb_list_registered_graphs · Public sink: brainkb_login, brainkb_whoami, brainkb_ingest_text, brainkb_list_uploads, brainkb_upload_status, brainkb_discard_upload, brainkb_ingest_upload, brainkb_add_access_rule, brainkb_list_users, brainkb_assign_role, brainkb_remove_role, brainkb_activate_user, brainkb_deactivate_user, brainkb_ban_user, brainkb_unban_user · Destructive: brainkb_add_space_graph, brainkb_ingest_text, brainkb_discard_upload, brainkb_sparql, brainkb_remove_access_rule, brainkb_remove_role, brainkb_ban_user

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
